properties.displayName: QC - D - Suspicious Terminal Services service started
properties.description:
This query identifies any new service started utilizing the net command. Additionally, it looks for the particular
case of Terminal Services (TermService) service enabling.
Adversaries may abuse the Windows service control manager to execute malicious commands
or payloads. The Windows service control manager (services.exe) is an interface to manage and manipulate services.
The service control manager is accessible to users via GUI components as well as system utilities such as sc.exe
and Net. Adversaries may try to get information about registered services. Commands that may obtain information
about services using operating system utilities are "sc," "tasklist /svc" using Tasklist, and "net start" using Net,
but adversaries may also use other tools as well. Adversaries may use the information from System Service Discovery
during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target
and/or attempts specific actions.
Reference:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1007/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0039/
  - https://www.windows-commandline.com/start-terminal-services-command-line/
properties.query:
let net_params = dynamic (["start TermService"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType has "ProcessCreated"
| where FileName has_any ("net", "net1") 
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (net_params)
| summarize FileName = make_set(FileName), ProcessId = make_set(ProcessId), InitiatingProcessParentId = make_set(InitiatingProcessParentId), InitiatingProcessId = make_set(InitiatingProcessId), 
          count() by DeviceName, ActionType, 
                      InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,  
                      InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, 
                      AccountDomain, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation
| project-reorder DeviceName, ActionType, 
                InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,  FileName, 
                ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessParentId, InitiatingProcessId,
                ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, 
                AccountDomain, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation
